articles.title: IPL: MI, PBKS in talks over Hardik Pandya, Arshdeep Singh trade
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The IPL trading window has sprung to life with a potential blockbuster deal involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The IPL trading window has sprung to life with a potential blockbuster deal involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh. TOI has learnt that the Punjab Kings (PBKS) and Mumbai Indians (MI) are engaged in advanced discussions over a trade that could see India's premier left-arm seamer move to Mumbai in exchange for the star all-rounder ahead of the IPL auction next month."Talks involving Hardik are at an advanced stage between Punjab Kings and MI. If PBKS part with Arshdeep to acquire Hardik, they could look to bring in a left-arm pacer from another franchise or target one at the auction. However, nothing has been finalised yet," a source tracking developments told TOI.Hardik's future has emerged as the biggest talking point of the trading season. TOI understands that Rajasthan Royals, Kolkata Knight Riders and Lucknow Super Giants have also expressed interest in acquiring him. "The challenge for any franchise is that Mumbai Indians are unlikely to let Hardik go without receiving proven core players in return," a source said. "A lot of movement in the trade market could depend on where Hardik ends up. One deal could trigger several others as teams look to fill the gaps created by such a trade."As part of their efforts to secure Hardik, PBKS could consider releasing players such as Marcus Stoinis and Nehal Wadhera ahead of the mini-auction on Dec 16. Hardik would join Punjab solely as a player, with Shreyas Iyer set to continue as skipper.With the BCCI extending the trade window deadline to November 17, all parties still have time to finalise what could be one of the most significant player moves in IPL history.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘I would love to work with them’: Suresh Raina makes big CSK revelation, awaits franchise’s call
articles.summary: Former India batter Suresh Raina has expressed his desire to return to Chennai Super Kings (CSK), this time as a member of their coaching staff, after
articles.body: Former India batter Suresh Raina has expressed his desire to return to Chennai Super Kings (CSK), this time as a member of their coaching staff, after revealing that he has approached the franchise for a role but is yet to receive a response.Raina, popularly known as ‘Mr IPL’, was a key figure in CSK's journey in the Indian Premier League (IPL), representing the franchise from 2008 to 2021. He remains the leading run-scorer for the Chennai-based side in T20 cricket, having amassed 5,529 runs in 200 matches.A four-time IPL champion and two-time Champions League winner with CSK, Raina has taken up roles as an expert and commentator since retiring from professional cricket. However, he is now keen to contribute to the franchise off the field.Speaking during a conversation with his former India and CSK teammate Ravichandran Ashwin, Raina said his years of experience, performances in high-pressure situations and contribution to the team's success had prompted him to seek a coaching opportunity.“I’ve played almost 16 or 17 years in the IPL. I’ve scored enough for us (CSK), played in finals, and handled a lot of high-pressure games. I’ve asked them (CSK), and now it’s on them to decide. It’s their team now – we (Raina and Ashwin) are both retired, so they have to make the call," Raina said.“We’ve done our part, won trophies, and lifted titles together. Now, they need to see how we can contribute to CSK. I’ve been playing since day one, so if they feel I’m capable," he added.The former left-handed batter made it clear that he is open to taking up any responsibility within the CSK set-up. For Raina, continuing his association with the franchise and being part of another trophy-winning campaign would matter more than the designation.“I would love to work with them in any capacity! For me, as long as I’m with the boys and they’re winning trophies, that’s what matters – because yellow is everything to us," Raina said.Raina also explained that he wants to pass on the lessons gathered from years of playing international cricket, World Cups and the IPL to the next generation. Having featured in several finals and experienced both victories and defeats, he believes he can help players deal with the mental demands of the tournament.“I’ve played international cricket, the IPL, and World Cups, so I’ve experienced every side of the game. I know what kind of pressure you face, especially when playing so many finals—winning some, losing some. I’ve learned how to handle that pressure and how to get the best out of yourself mentally. We must have played nine or ten finals together and won four of them. I’m still the highest run-scorer in IPL playoffs, so I know what I’ve achieved in this tournament, and I just want to give that back to the players," Raina said.He also pointed out that while CSK have embraced an aggressive style of cricket, players still need guidance on handling pressure, maintaining consistency and managing their workload across demanding seasons.“They’re doing really well and playing an aggressive, different brand of cricket, Ash. But they still need someone who can guide them on managing stress and workload. It’s not about lecturing them on technique—it’s all about how to stay consistent season after season, and that’s what truly matters," he added.Meanwhile, CSK have made significant changes to their coaching staff ahead of the 2027 IPL season. Former India pacer Zaheer Khan has taken over as head coach, succeeding Stephen Fleming, while Mohit Sharma has been appointed bowling coach. Gareth Batty and Albie Morkel have also joined the five-time IPL champions as assistant coaches.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Anshul Kamboj joins Jasprit Bumrah in elite list after record-breaking spell against New Zealand
articles.summary: Anshul Kamboj produced a remarkable turnaround in his second ODI appearance, delivering a disciplined spell to help India bowl out New Zealand for 185 in
articles.body: Anshul Kamboj produced a remarkable turnaround in his second ODI appearance, delivering a disciplined spell to help India bowl out New Zealand for 185 in the series opener at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday.The Haryana pacer, who endured a difficult debut against the West Indies in New Chandigarh last month, bounced back in style with figures of 2/22 in his 10 overs. His economy rate of 2.20 stood out in an impressive collective bowling effort as India restricted the hosts to 185 in 40.2 overs after opting to bowl first.Kamboj had conceded 82 runs without taking a wicket in his 10 overs on debut, as the West Indies successfully chased down a target of 352 by five wickets. However, there was little sign of that outing affecting his confidence in Auckland, where his accuracy, ability to extract bounce and subtle seam movement troubled the New Zealand batters.Bowling first change, the 25-year-old kept things tight through the middle overs and picked up the wickets of New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner and Nathan Smith. His figures also earned him a place in the record books.Kamboj's economy rate of 2.20 is the best by an Indian pacer since Jasprit Bumrah recorded identical figures against Zimbabwe in Harare in 2016.Ashish Nehra was the first to achieve the feat against Sri Lanka in Dambulla in August 2005, returning figures of 2/22. Ajit Agarkar matched it against the West Indies in Kuala Lumpur in September 2006, while Bumrah registered 4/22 against Zimbabwe in June 2016.Best economy for an India pacer in an ODI innings since 2005:BowlerFiguresOppositionYearAshish Nehra2/22Sri Lanka2005Ajit Agarkar2/22West Indies2006Jasprit Bumrah4/22Zimbabwe2016Anshul Kamboj2/22New Zealand2026India's bowling attack delivered a collective performance, with all five bowlers used by captain Shubman Gill contributing to the effort. Arshdeep Singh led the attack with four wickets, while Gurnoor Brar claimed three. Kamboj picked up two wickets, and Axar Patel provided valuable support with his spin.Arshdeep made early inroads, dismissing openers Will Young and Henry Nicholls, while Brar removed Tim Latham with a sharp reflex catch off his own bowling. Tim Seifert, who scored 38, also fell after mistiming a pull shot.Daryl Mitchell looked comfortable during his 28-run stay before being run out following a sharp throw from Rohit Sharma. New Zealand struggled to build substantial partnerships as India's bowlers maintained pressure throughout the innings.Axar troubled Santner with his spin before Kamboj eventually bowled the New Zealand captain. The pacer then accounted for Nathan Smith, who fell to a stunning one-handed catch by Virat Kohli.Glenn Phillips offered some resistance with 30 runs before Arshdeep returned to dismiss him. However, Blair Tickner provided late fireworks, smashing 34 off 23 balls, including four sixes, in a 39-run last-wicket partnership with Jacob Duffy.Despite the late assault, India wrapped up the New Zealand innings at 185, with Kamboj's impressive comeback emerging as one of the major positives for the visitors.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Virat Kohli scripts history in Auckland, becomes first batter to achieve this feat
articles.summary: Virat Kohli added another remarkable milestone to his illustrious career on Wednesday, becoming the first batter in ODI history to score 13,000 runs while
articles.body: Virat Kohli added another remarkable milestone to his illustrious career on Wednesday, becoming the first batter in ODI history to score 13,000 runs while batting at the No. 3 position.The former India captain achieved the landmark during the first ODI against New Zealand at Eden Park in Auckland, further strengthening his standing as one of the greatest one-day batters of all time.Kohli reached the milestone in a category dominated by some of the biggest names in cricket. Before him, only Sachin Tendulkar had crossed the 13,000-run mark at a single batting position in ODIs, having scored 13,685 runs while batting at No. 2.Kohli now leads the list of highest run-scorers at No. 3 with exactly 13,000 runs at an outstanding average of 61.61. Former Australia captain Ricky Ponting is second on the list with 12,662 runs at 42.48, followed by Sri Lanka great Kumar Sangakkara, who accumulated 9,747 runs at 44.71.South Africa's Jacques Kallis occupies fourth place with 7,774 runs, while New Zealand's Kane Williamson is fifth with 6,504. Pakistan's Babar Azam and England's Joe Root complete the list of the top seven run-scorers at the position.Most runs at No. 3 in ODI cricketBatterRunsAverageVirat Kohli13,00061.61Ricky Ponting12,66242.48Kumar Sangakkara9,74744.71Jacques Kallis7,77445.72Kane Williamson6,50451.61Babar Azam6,05455.54Joe Root5,52553.12Kohli returned to India's ODI playing XI for the series opener alongside Rohit Sharma and KL Rahul, for the five-match ODI series.India, meanwhile, made a strong start with the ball after captain Shubman Gill elected to bowl first. The visitors dismissed New Zealand for 185 in 40.2 overs, with Arshdeep Singh claiming four wickets, Gurnoor Brar taking three and Anshul Kamboj picking up two.Kohli also made his presence felt in the field, taking a spectacular one-handed catch to dismiss Nathan Smith off Kamboj's bowling.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Can't see the ball': Virat Kohli, Shubman Gill angry as play continues in rain in Auckland
articles.summary: India captain Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli appeared unhappy as play continued despite rain during the first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland on
articles.body: India captain Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli appeared unhappy as play continued despite rain during the first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland on Wednesday.The match was initially stopped in the 11th over of India's chase of 186, with the visitors at 29/1. Kohli was batting on 29, while Gill was on 17.Play resumed after a delay of more than an hour, with India's target revised to 167 under the DLS method. However, rain returned after only a few deliveries had been bowled.As the umpires looked to complete the 12th over, both Kohli and Gill appeared reluctant to continue in the conditions. Before the final delivery of the over, Kohli smiled and told umpire Paul Reiffel, "Look at the sightscreen, can't see the ball," before making a double teapot gesture.Gill also spoke to the square-leg umpire to make his point, but the officials appeared keen to complete the over. Meanwhile, New Zealand bowler Blair Tickner pulled his shirt over his head, seemingly in jest, as Gill took his time to get ready.Gill survived the final delivery before play was stopped again, with India at 64/1 after 12 overs.FOLLOW LIVEGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: AK47 finds the target: Relentless Anshul Kamboj reaps benefits of better planning
articles.summary: AUCKLAND: A day before members of India's ODI squad were scheduled to train at the Eden Park, Anshul Kamboj was out for a stroll with Ruturaj Gaikwad.
articles.body: AUCKLAND: A day before members of India's ODI squad were scheduled to train at the Eden Park, Anshul Kamboj was out for a stroll with Ruturaj Gaikwad. The two grabbed a quick bite at a fast-food joint near a busy setting for a Diwali fair, obliged fans with some pictures, and then slipped out largely unnoticed. The 25-year-old Kamboj, still four sleeps away from eventually his second ODI appearance, looked relaxed following proper training, adequate rest and timely communication.The right-arm seamer would bowl relentlessly to the likes of Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma in the nets on November 1, enjoy a bowling rest the following day, and then apply the finishing touches on the eve of the seriesopener against New Zealand.Given his chaotic entry into Test and ODI cricket, the preparations felt too good to be true. Much like his dreamy outing in the series opener against the Black Caps.Kamboj has had forgettable outings in international cricket but he ensured Auckland didn't follow the pattern. With relentless lengths, sharp use of the wobble seam and speeds, the highly-rated Haryana bowler showed why the management didn't give up on him. Throughout his spells, Kamboj didn't miss his spot even when the opponents tried to unsettle him by charging down the ground, reaping rewards both for himself and the team for his persistence.‘’One match doesn’t decide a career… I have been doing same things. I got motivation to do well after Manchester Test. I dont pay attention to outside talk,’’ Kamboj said at the post-match press conference.When you prepare well, it gives you confidence so and ensures there are no surprises in the match,” he said about the preparation.When Kamboj sucked the momentum out of the New Zealand batting, Gurnoor Brar and Arshdeep Singh added to the wickets tally from the other end. Nearly half the Kiwi side was back in the hut when Kamboj finished his first spell (5-1-12-0) — leaving the hosts' hopes of a big total to a lower-order miracle. Axar Patel was introduced to give the seamers a breather and the short break further fired up Kamboj as he cranked up speeds flirting around the 140 kmph mark in his second spell.“Dimensions were different but it doesn’t matter when there is help off the pitch,” Kamboj said about the venue.The relentlessness paid off as he picked the wickets of Mitchell Santner and Nathan Smith in consecutive overs, leaving mere formalities to be completed. The next five overs improved upon the first spell, capping off an incisive spell of fast bowling. The unfamiliar feelingAuckland must have given Kamboj an unfamiliar feeling, as he isn't used to normalcy as far as international cricket is concerned. This time, however, the preparation and planning were spot on. He wasn't an injury replacement taking a long international flight or switching formats after a quick flight from South to East India.The plan to give up on him after ordinary Test and ODI debuts was never on the table as the management always believed in his abilities. When he returned to the set-up after the Manchester Test, his increased pace immediately caught attention. The think-tank was impressed with the drastic improvement and was keen on giving him consistent gametime even after the Guwahati ODI against West Indies.When the Windies took Kamboj to the cleaners, India captain Shubman Gill backed the under-fire quick and asserted that both Auqib Nabi and Kamboj would continue to be in the mix.“It's not easy to come and be able to deliver straight away,” Gill had said.“Anshul and Auqib are the kind of players who are going to be in the mix a lot. And Anshul is someone who can also bat at number 8. And that number is very crucial for us,” he further added.Selectors heard the captain, kept the two in the mix and with meticulous planning, helped Haryana's AK47 find the target. Short, good lengths were the order of the day and with razor sharp precision, Kamboj hit the spot to keep India on top. Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sachin Tendulkar's record gone! Virat Kohli creates history during India's New Zealand chase
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli continued to rewrite the record books on Wednesday, breaking Sachin Tendulkar's long-standing record for the most runs in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli continued to rewrite the record books on Wednesday, breaking Sachin Tendulkar's long-standing record for the most runs in successful and unsuccessful ODI run chases during India's rain-affected first ODI against New Zealand at Eden Park in Auckland.The former India captain produced another masterclass in chasing, scoring a fluent 74 off just 51 deliveries as India overhauled a revised target of 143 in 22.4 overs in a contest reduced to 32 overs per side by rain. Kohli's innings, which featured 13 fours and a six, set the tone for India's chase after an early setback.With his knock, Kohli took his tally of runs in ODI chases to 8,741, moving past Tendulkar's previous record of 8,720. He now stands alone at the top of the all-time list, further strengthening his reputation as one of the greatest chase masters the game has witnessed.The numbers underline Kohli's remarkable consistency in this format. He has scored his 8,741 runs in chases at an average of 66.21 and a strike rate of 95.03. Tendulkar, meanwhile, finished with 8,720 runs at an average of 42.33 and a strike rate of 88.44.Kohli equals Ponting's record against New ZealandThe 37-year-old added another significant milestone to his ODI career, equalling Ricky Ponting's record for the most runs against New Zealand in the format.Kohli now has 1,971 ODI runs against the Black Caps, drawing level with the former Australia captain, who accumulated the same number during his illustrious career. With more matches remaining in the ongoing series, Kohli has an opportunity to move past Ponting and claim the record outright.Former India great Tendulkar is third on the list with 1,750 runs against New Zealand, followed by Sri Lanka's Kumar Sangakkara (1,568) and Sanath Jayasuriya (1,519).Most ODI runs against New Zealand1971 - Virat Kohli1971 - Ricky Ponting1750 - Sachin Tendulkar1568 - Kumar Sangakkara1519 - Sanath Jayasuriya1449 - Jacques KallisFirst batter to reach 13,000 ODI runs at No. 3Kohli also became the first batter in ODI history to reach 13,000 runs while batting at the No. 3 position.He achieved the landmark during his innings against New Zealand, taking his tally at the position to exactly 13,000 at an extraordinary average of 61.61.Before Kohli, only Tendulkar had crossed the 13,000-run mark at a particular batting position in ODI cricket. The Master Blaster scored 13,685 runs while batting at No. 2.Kohli now leads the list of leading run-scorers at No. 3, comfortably ahead of Ponting, who finished with 12,662 runs, and Sangakkara, who accumulated 9,747.Most ODI runs at No. 3Virat Kohli - 13,000*Ricky Ponting - 12,662Kumar Sangakkara - 9,747Jacques Kallis - 7,774Kane Williamson - 6,504Kohli-Gill partnership puts India in controlKohli's milestones came during a commanding partnership with Shubman Gill, who helped India recover after Rohit Sharma departed in the opening over.The duo stitched together a crucial 113-run stand for the second wicket, taking control of a tricky chase that had already been interrupted by rain. While Gill took time to settle in, Kohli looked in sublime touch, finding gaps regularly and punishing loose deliveries through the off-side and square-leg regions.Kohli accelerated after the first rain interruption, but his entertaining knock eventually ended in the 20th over when he attempted to pull Jacob Duffy's short delivery. He failed to control the shot and was caught by Tim Seifert at deep backward square leg for 74.India did lose a few wickets in quick succession towards the end, but with fewer than 30 runs required, the result was never seriously in doubt.It was another vintage Kohli performance — a combination of composure, controlled aggression and remarkable consistency — as India began the New Zealand ODI series with a victory.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mitchell Starc dethrones Marco Jansen to reclaim No.1 spot in ICC Test rankings
articles.summary: Australia's pace spearhead Mitchell Starc has climbed back to the summit of the ICC Test bowling rankings, dethroning South Africa's Marco Jansen
articles.body: Australia's pace spearhead Mitchell Starc has climbed back to the summit of the ICC Test bowling rankings, dethroning South Africa's Marco Jansen following a prolific series with the ball.At 36, Starc continues to underline his value as one of the most formidable fast bowlers in the longest format, having finished as the leading wicket-taker in Australia's recently concluded three-Test series against South Africa with 15 wickets.Despite Australia losing the series 2-1, Starc's individual performances proved exceptional. The left-arm pacer produced a remarkable effort in the final Test, claiming nine wickets, including an impressive 6/72 in the first innings.Starc ends Jansen's brief reign; Harmer makes big jumpJansen had moved to the No.1 position in both the Test bowling and all-rounder rankings just last week following an outstanding performance with bat and ball in the second Test. However, Starc's exploits in the series finale have pushed the Australian back ahead of the South African.Meanwhile, South Africa spinner Simon Harmer was another major beneficiary of the latest rankings update. The off-spinner climbed nine places to seventh after producing a memorable performance in the third Test, where he claimed his maiden 10-wicket match haul and was named Player of the Match.Australia lose series despite Starc's brillianceSouth Africa clinched the three-match Test series 2-1 after defeating Australia in the deciding third Test. The hosts bounced back from their defeat in the opening match to win the next two Tests and secure a memorable series triumph.While Starc's nine-wicket performance in the final Test kept Australia in contention, South Africa held their nerve to seal the contest. The series also saw Jansen emerge as a major force with both bat and ball, while Harmer's match-winning 10-wicket haul proved decisive in the final encounter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'He was annoying': Jacob Duffy's hilarious take on Virat Kohli after India's Auckland victory
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: New Zealand pacer Jacob Duffy had a rather amusing assessment of Virat Kohli after the India batting great once again proved to be the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: New Zealand pacer Jacob Duffy had a rather amusing assessment of Virat Kohli after the India batting great once again proved to be the difference between the two sides in the first ODI at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday. Kohli smashed a fluent 74 off just 51 balls to guide India to a five-wicket victory in a rain-affected contest, leaving Duffy impressed and, by his own admission, a little frustrated.Asked about Kohli's batting, Duffy did not hold back, responding with a smile: "He was annoying (laughs). Not many holes in his game… small ground, uses the pace very well."The New Zealand pacer acknowledged the challenge of bowling to the former India captain, whose ability to exploit the dimensions of Eden Park and use the pace of the deliveries made life difficult for the hosts.Kohli's innings featured 13 fours and a six as India chased down a revised target of 143 in 22.4 overs in a match reduced to 32 overs per side following rain interruptions.ALSO READ: Sachin Tendulkar's record gone! Virat Kohli creates history during India's New Zealand chase'180 at Eden Park was never going to be enough'Reflecting on New Zealand's batting performance, Duffy admitted that the hosts had fallen short of a competitive total after being bowled out for 180."180 at Eden Park was never going to be enough. They bowled pretty well. We showed our intent for the series that we won’t back down," he said.Duffy also credited the Indian bowling attack for making life difficult for the New Zealand batters."India bowled well, extracted the bounce very well. We are a good batting team," he said.Despite the defeat, the pacer insisted that New Zealand would continue to play with an aggressive approach throughout the series.Duffy impressed by India's players and fansDuffy also spoke about his admiration for Indian players, highlighting their patience and appreciation of the support they receive from fans."A lot of Indian players are patient, appreciate their fans. I look up to them… impressive to watch," he said.The New Zealand pacer also touched upon the decision not to use captain Mitchell Santner as a bowling option, pointing to the conditions at Eden Park."Eden Park bounce extracts the wicket," Duffy said.Meanwhile, Kohli's match-winning contribution was accompanied by several significant milestones. He surpassed Sachin Tendulkar's record for the most ODI runs in run chases, taking his tally to 8,741, against Tendulkar's 8,720.The 37-year-old also became the first batter to score 13,000 ODI runs at No. 3 and equalled Ricky Ponting's record of 1,971 ODI runs against New Zealand.India will look to carry the momentum into the second ODI as Kohli's record-breaking performance gives the visitors an early advantage in the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'One match doesn't decide a career': Anshul Kamboj's strong response after match-winning show against New Zealand
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Anshul Kamboj had a message for his critics after delivering an impressive performance in India's opening ODI against New Zealand at Eden Park
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Anshul Kamboj had a message for his critics after delivering an impressive performance in India's opening ODI against New Zealand at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday. The Haryana pacer, who was named Player of the Match for his disciplined spell of 2/22 in 10 overs, made it clear that he was not allowing outside opinions to affect his approach, insisting that one performance should not define a player's career."One match doesn’t decide a career… I have been doing the same things. I got motivation to do well after the Manchester Test. I don't pay attention to outside talk," Kamboj said during the post-match press conference.The 25-year-old's comments came after he played a crucial role in India's bowling dominance, helping the visitors dismiss New Zealand for 185 before they completed a five-wicket victory in the rain-affected contest.Kamboj removed New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner for four and Nathan Smith for one, delivering a disciplined performance alongside Arshdeep Singh, who claimed four wickets, and Gurnoor Brar, who picked up three.Wobble seam and disciplined lengths key to successExplaining the secret behind his impressive figures, Kamboj credited his ability to stick to the basics rather than getting distracted by the nature of the surface."I think the key was just consistent length and line, not thinking about how the wicket is behaving, just the basic plan, bowling on right lines and right areas," he said in the post-match presentations.The pacer also revealed that the wobble seam delivery proved particularly effective against the New Zealand batters."I think the wobble seam ball was working very well, so I was using that again and again," he said.Kamboj explained that his preparations involved working on his lengths and studying the strengths and weaknesses of opposition batters."Just working on lengths and good lines, and just looking at the strengths and weaknesses of the batsmen and just working on that," he added.He also stressed that preparation was important in building confidence ahead of a match during the press briefing: "When you prepare well, it gives you confidence and ensures there are no surprises in the match."'Dimensions were different but...'Asked about adjusting to New Zealand conditions and the different dimensions at Eden Park, Kamboj said his focus remained on executing his plans rather than making unnecessary changes."Dimensions were different but it doesn’t matter when there is help off the pitch," he said.The all-rounder also spoke about balancing his responsibilities with both bat and ball, keeping his approach straightforward."All rounder roles are simple: focus on batting when bat in hand, bowling when ball in hand," he said during the PC.Kamboj's performance was part of a collective bowling effort that set up India's victory. In reply, Virat Kohli smashed 74 off 51 balls, while Shubman Gill scored 56 off 37 deliveries as India chased down the rain-revised target of 143 in 22.4 overs.India will now look to extend their advantage in the five-match series when the second ODI takes place in Wellington on Saturday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tanush Kotian's 7/45 against Railways strengthens India Test selection case ahead of Australia series
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Tanush Kotian turned in another superlative performance on Wednesday to stay in the reckoning for a spot in the India Test team when Australia
articles.body: MUMBAI: Tanush Kotian turned in another superlative performance on Wednesday to stay in the reckoning for a spot in the India Test team when Australia visit for a five-match series next year.The off-spinner, who took career-best figures of 8/81 against Haryana in the last match, finished with 7/45 against Railways as Mumbai skittled them out for 259, taking a 137-run first innings lead at the Brabourne Stadium.At stumps, half-centuries from Angkrish Raghuvanshi (79, 85b; 10x4, 1x6) and Divyaansh Sksena (68 not out, 114b; 6x4) guided the 42-time champions to 174/4, stretching their lead to 311 and putting them on the verge of a fourth straight outright win.The two big performances with the ball, besides his valuable contributions with the bat, mean it will be difficult for the national selectors to ignore him. The competition for the off-spinner's spot is tough, with Washington Sundar the team's first choice and Saransh Jain also in contention after playing in the Sri Lanka series.Kotian, though, is keeping his head down and taking wickets to keep himself in fray. This season, he has taken 37 wickets in seven first-class matches, including 22 in four Ranji Trophy games, an eight-wicket match haul for West Zone in the Duleep Trophy, and seven wickets in two matches for India A against Australia A.Asked whether he is close to earning an India Test cap, Kotian said: "I think I am close. But let's see... it's their (national selectors') call in the end. I have to do my things and do them correctly. I will be ready till then."Right now, he is treating every outing as an opportunity to improve his bowling and implement the new tricks he added to his armour during the off-season, including effective use of the crease, angles and variations."This game I used the straighter one effectively, which got me a couple of lbws," said Kotian, who has been included in the India A squad for the ACC Men's Rising Stars Asia Cup in Doha from Nov 10 to 29.He also displayed the maturity to adapt to different surfaces, besides showing patience when things did not go his way. In the past, Kotian was guilty of bowling with a flatter trajectory, but experience and working with different coaches over the years have helped him understand the nuances of the art of spin."In the last game (against Haryana), it was turning a lot. On this wicket, it was not gripping that much. Being accurate and building pressure was crucial in this game. Bowling maidens and putting pressure on the batters made them play rash shots and I got those wickets," explained Kotian.In the past, Kotian was brought on mostly when left-handers were batting, but on Wednesday he showed that he is equally capable of toppling right-handers as five of his seven scalps came against them. That can be an useful indicator of his versatility when selectors sit down to pick the team for the Australia series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ace and pace do it for India: Kohli conquers Eden Park, pacers run riot in rain-hit win over New Zealand
articles.summary: There are days when a difficult pitch makes batting look like hard work.
articles.body: There are days when a difficult pitch makes batting look like hard work. And then there are days when Virat Kohli walks out and makes it look like an entirely different sport.At Eden Park, Auckland, on Wednesday, as New Zealand's seamers found bounce and movement on a responsive pitch, and batters from both sides struggled to find their bearings, Kohli seemed to be operating on another plane. There was no apparent fuss, no visible discomfort, just a succession of crisp strokes, authoritative pulls and drives that made a challenging surface look deceptively easy. His 74 off just 51 balls provided the decisive flourish as India wrapped up a five-wicket DLS victory over New Zealand in a rain-hit first ODI.The result, however, was set up by a relentless Indian pace attack that had dismantled New Zealand for 185 in 40.2 overs. Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar and Anshul Kamboj combined to make life difficult for the home batters, while Shubman Gill's attacking captaincy and India's outstanding work in the field ensured there was hardly any room for New Zealand to recover. The frequent rain interruptions during India's chase made the damage done with the ball in the first innings even more significant.Just four days back, New Zealand had piled up 259 in the fourth T20I at the same venue. On Wednesday, on a surface offering considerable assistance to the seamers, they found themselves unable to withstand India's four-pronged pace assault.Kamboj, preferred over the experienced Mohammed Siraj, was arguably the standout of the Indian attack, finishing with figures of 2/22 in his 10 overs. He kept extracting movement and maintained impeccable control even deep into his final spell.Arshdeep had already made the early inroads, using the short-of-good-length ball to unsettle Will Young and Henry Nicholls, both of whom top-edged their attempted responses.Gurnoor, meanwhile, brought his own brand of hostility. Tim Seifert, who top-scored with 38, fell to another mistimed pull off Gurnoor's bowling, while Tom Latham offered a sharp return catch to the bowler.The fielding matched the bowling's intensity. Rohit Sharma produced a superb diving run-out to send back Daryl Mitchell, while Kohli, a day short of his 38th birthday, pulled off a stunning one-handed catch at second slip to dismiss Nathan Smith off Kamboj. Gill, too, was proactive with his bowling changes, refusing to let the pressure ease.Arshdeep, in his pursuit of a five-wicket haul, did allow No. 11 Blair Tickner to strike three sixes and inflate his figures to 4/70, but Gurnoor ensured the last-wicket resistance did not stretch any further with another lifter that got the better of Tickner.If the Indian bowlers made the first half of the match their own, Kohli ensured the second belonged to him. Rohit Sharma fell for a duck in the first over of the chase, unable to keep an off-drive down. Skipper Gill, despite looking composed, could not find the fluency that is often attached to his batting.Yet Kohli appeared untroubled by the very conditions that had made batting such a demanding exercise for everyone else. There is a freshness about Kohli's batting at the moment, an unmistakable willingness to take the initiative rather than wait for the game to unfold. His intent was evident in the way he took on Tickner, repeatedly putting away short deliveries with disdain. The New Zealand pacers tried to use the extra bounce to test him, but Kohli seemed to have an answer for everything. He pulled with authority, drove on the up and found the gaps with the sort of precision that comes from complete conviction.Gill (37 off 56) offered valuable support but could hardly match Kohli. When the Indian captain fell, a mini collapse followed, with four wickets going down for 22 runs, including Kohli's dismissal. By then, however, the damage had been done to New Zealand.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Leicestershire relegation confirmed after appeal against points deduction dismissed
articles.summary: Leicestershire's relegation from Division One of the County Championship is confirmed after failing in their appeal against a points penalty.
articles.body:
Leicestershire's relegation from Division One of the County Championship has been confirmed after failing in their appeal against a points penalty.

It was during the penultimate match of the season in mid-September that the independent cricket discipline panel handed down an initial 27-point punishment for the poor pitch they produced against Glamorgan a month earlier.

Leicestershire were stripped of all 19 points earned in the win over Glamorgan and hit with an extra eight-point penalty - as well as a further suspended eight-point deduction and £5,000 fine.

That dropped them to the bottom of the table before they were eventually relegated - pending their appeal - eight days later.

Their appeal appeared to get a boost soon after the season ended when they had eight points reinstated after the Cricket Regulator raised questions with the discipline panel.

For more than five weeks, however, Leicestershire's relegation and the survival of Essex, who finished 17 points above the Foxes, remained in limbo.

The appeals panel upheld the disciplinary tribunal's decision to dock Leicestershire the 19 points earned in the win against Glamorgan after they "failed to show it had acted reasonably in preparing the pitch", which was rated as "poor" and deemed "sub-standard".

The panel also rejected Leicestershire's attempt to bring forward fresh evidence - presented by the Pakistan Cricket Board's chief curator Tony Hemmings - by stating "the club is the author of its own misfortune".

The panel's "view" was that there "appears to have been a woeful lack of understanding" of regulations by those in charge at Leicestershire.

"TH's (Hemmings') evidence was reasonably available at the time of that hearing and we reject [Leicestershire's legal representative] Mr Harris' submission to the contrary," the panel said in its findings. , external

"The senior executives at a professional cricket club should be familiar with the regulations, or at least to remind themselves of them as circumstances may require. That was not done here."

Leicestershire chief executive Emma White said it was "deeply frustrating" that the expert evidence was not heard, adding that the club "felt rushed and under considerable pressure throughout this process".

"We are hugely disappointed by this outcome, but we will not allow it to define us," she added in a statement on the club website. , external

How Bollywood played part in Foxes drama

Leicestershire's 42-run victory against Glamorgan on 23 August was just their second of the season and they thought it would aid their battle to avoid an immediate return to the second tier.

But the condition of pitch, which Glamorgan head coach Richard Dawson described at the time as "tough" for batters, immediately came under scrutiny as match officials asked for the England and Wales Cricket Board's pitch and grounds advisor Andy Mackay to carry out an inspection after the game finished.

The highest team score in the match was Leicestershire's 257 all out in their second innings.

While Leicestershire head coach Alfonso Thomas argued that the surface had been prepared in the same way as the pitch used against Yorkshire - a game the Foxes won by an innings and 39 runs in June - he also acknowledged it was "a bit drier than what we wanted" for the match against Glamorgan.

Leicestershire's head groundsman Callum Lewin went on to tell the cricket regulator there were "circumstances leading up to the game that were just out of my control".

It included the exceptionally hot summer weather, as well as an "unscheduled Bollywood filming event" that took place at Uptonsteel Grace Road days before the match started.

It was said "the arrangements for this had been chaotic", with another member of the ground staff, Mark Smith, saying the 13 hours that the pitch was left uncovered was "crazy".

Foxes CEO White said the grounds team has her "full support" and added "I remain immensely proud of the work they do".

"Come pre-season, we will be ready to battle it out in Division Two, and to fight our way back," she continued.

articles.title: Late starts, moisture making it difficult to defend totals: Jacob Duffy
articles.summary: New Zealand pacer Jacob Duffy identified late match starts and evening moisture as significant factors behind the hosts’ repeated struggles to defend
articles.body: New Zealand pacer Jacob Duffy identified late match starts and evening moisture as significant factors behind the hosts’ repeated struggles to defend totals in the ongoing home series against India.India took a 1-0 lead in the five-match ODI series at Eden Park, Auckland, bundling the Black Caps out for 185 before comfortably chasing down a rain-revised target of 143 in 32 overs on Wednesday. The defeat marked the fourth instance in five games across formats on this tour where New Zealand failed to defend a total after losing the toss and being inserted to bat.With ODIs scheduled for 3 pm starts following the 8 pm T20I fixtures, Duffy noted how second-innings conditions make it easy for batting."Everyone wins the toss and bowls first for a reason," Duffy said. "I'm not saying it's impossible to defend, don't get me wrong. It's not like we're giving up as soon as we've lost a toss. But as soon as you get a little bit of moisture in the wicket — I thought tonight there was a bit of wind around and we actually might not get that moisture, but I guess the rain sort of adds that moisture that the dew would have otherwise."When it does skid on like that, it sort of takes away the tackiness and that sort of tennis-bally bounce we saw in their (India's) innings."Duffy admitted 185 was "never going to be enough" at Eden Park, crediting India’s pace trio of Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar and Anshul Kamboj for extracting movement and steep bounce."They bowled really well. They've got some big boys in that bowling attack, and they used the bounce of the surface really well," Duffy said. "We probably just weren't at our best with the bat to start with, and then it's pretty tough to defend 180."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From Chandigarh nightmare to Auckland redemption, Anshul Kamboj turns a corner
articles.summary: Anshul Kamboj had every reason to remember his ODI debut, not necessarily fondly.
articles.body: Anshul Kamboj had every reason to remember his ODI debut, not necessarily fondly. On Oct 3, the Haryana pacer went wicketless and conceded 82 runs in nine overs against the West Indies in New Chandigarh, a performance that put him in the list of most expensive Indian bowlers on ODI debut. On Wednesday, at Eden Park, he had a rather different story to tell.In his first over itself, Kamboj bowled a maiden to swashbuckling New Zealand opener Tim Seifert. After what he had endured in his maiden ODI, six balls without a run felt like a small victory in itself.By the end of the evening, Kamboj had collected two wickets, conceded just 22 runs in his 10 overs and walked away with the Player of the Match award in India's five-wicket victory. It equalled the most economical ten-over spell by an Indian quick since Javagal Srinath’s 3/13 against Zimbabwe in 2003."One bad match does not decide a player's career," Kamboj said afterwards. "I have been doing the same things right from the start. One bad match doesn't affect me much. It has only given me the motivation to do better. I don't pay attention to the chatter. I focus on my cricket and see how I can improve."Until Auckland, Kamboj’s brief flirtation with international cricket had felt like a series of frantic, breathless airport scrambles. His Test debut in Manchester last year in July came after Arshdeep Singh suffered a split webbing during training. Kamboj arrived from India just days before the fourth Test against England and endured a difficult introduction, conceding 89 runs for one wicket in 18 overs. Ben Duckett and Zak Crawley made sure he had little time to settle.The ODI debut was no less abrupt. Called up as Prasidh Krishna's replacement after the Karnataka speedster injured his hamstring, Kamboj was pulled out of an India A fixture in Puducherry and drafted into the senior side against the West Indies.In Auckland, for the first time in his brief international career, he was not scrambling to join the squad or stepping in at the last minute. And when he was introduced as first change in the eighth over after India elected to bowl, he looked a bowler who knew exactly what he wanted to do.The conditions helped. Unlike the largely unresponsive surface in New Chandigarh, Eden Park offered enough seam movement to reward discipline. Kamboj found it immediately, extracting movement and hitting a testing length. Even when Seifert and Daryl Mitchell looked to attack, he refused to offer them anything easy.His first spell was wicketless but invaluable in building pressure. He returned later to remove New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner and Nathan Smith. His economy of 2.20 became the frugallest ten-over spell by an Indian seamer since Jasprit Bumrah’s identical figures against Zimbabwe in Harare ten years ago."In cricket, if you focus more on the process than the result, then you will be alright. If you are executing well, I mean if you want to bowl a yorker and if you execute well and still go for runs, then there's no problem. You don't focus on the result because the result won't always be in your favour. What you can do is you can execute well," he said."The feedback (after his ODI debut) was that if you are bowling in good areas, then you should continue it. It's not necessary that if you execute well every time, you will get hit for runs every time. So, just focus on your execution as much as possible. Don't think too much about the result."Kamboj was also quick to acknowledge that his contribution was part of a larger bowling effort. "If someone is bowling well from one end, then you get a wicket from the other end. You just have to create as much pressure as possible," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Heartbreaking defeat! Lizelle Lee's rare wicketkeeping error denies Hobart Hurricanes a Super Over against Melbourne Renegade - Watch
articles.summary: Melbourne Renegades pulled off a dramatic four-wicket victory over Hobart Hurricanes in the Women's Big Bash League (WBBL) on Wednesday, with a rare
articles.body: Melbourne Renegades pulled off a dramatic four-wicket victory over Hobart Hurricanes in the Women's Big Bash League (WBBL) on Wednesday, with a rare wicketkeeping infringement on the final delivery denying the hosts a chance to force a Super Over. Just when the Hurricanes appeared to have rescued a thrilling contest, Lizelle Lee's positioning behind the stumps turned the game on its head, handing the Renegades a victory through a no-ball decision at Bellerive Oval.Chasing 155, the Renegades needed one run from the final delivery with scores level at 154. Deandra Dottin failed to connect with Nicola Carey's delivery, and Lee collected the ball behind the stumps. Both teams appeared to be preparing for a Super Over, but the third umpire intervened after television replays showed that Lee had collected the ball in front of the stumps.Under Law 27.3, a wicketkeeper must remain wholly behind the striker's wicket until the ball touches the batter or their bat, passes the wicket, or the batter attempts a run. Any breach of this provision results in a no-ball being called. The decision awarded the Renegades the additional run they needed to seal a four-wicket win without a Super Over.Over-rate penalty adds to Hurricanes' late heartbreakThe dramatic finish followed another crucial twist in the final over. The Hurricanes were penalised for failing to complete their 20 overs within the stipulated time and were allowed only two fielders outside the 30-yard circle for the final three deliveries.After a dot ball, Dottin edged the penultimate delivery towards the deep third boundary. With the boundary rider unavailable because of the fielding restriction, the ball raced away for four, bringing the scores level at 154.Dottin then missed the final delivery, and Lee's infringement completed a remarkable turnaround for the visitors. The Hurricanes were left stunned as the Renegades celebrated their first victory of the WBBL|12 campaign.Nicola Carey, Chinelle Henry power Hurricanes to 154Earlier, Hobart Hurricanes posted 154/7 in their 20 overs, with captain Nicola Carey leading the charge in her 150th WBBL appearance. Carey struck 62 off 43 deliveries, providing stability to an innings that saw the Hurricanes lose wickets at regular intervals.West Indian all-rounder Chinelle Henry added a quickfire 36 off just 18 balls to give the hosts a late boost. However, Henry later hobbled off after bowling just one over, which cost 14 runs, with a suspected hip injury.Renegades captain Sophie Molineux led the bowling attack with figures of 4/22, taking her career WBBL tally to 101 wickets. She became only the second player in the franchise's history to reach the 100-wicket milestone, after Molly Strano.Hayley Matthews leads Renegades before late collapseIn reply, Hayley Matthews kept the Renegades on course with an impressive 59 off 44 deliveries, while Courtney Webb contributed 29 off 25 balls. The pair helped the visitors build a strong platform before the Hurricanes fought back.The Renegades suffered a dramatic collapse, losing five wickets for 37 runs after reaching 101, bringing the contest back into balance. Matthews was dismissed by Heather Graham, while Molly Strano produced a superb catch-and-bowl effort to remove Molineux.With 33 runs required from the final four overs, the Renegades used the Power Surge to keep the chase alive. Despite the late setbacks, they eventually crossed the line in one of the most unusual finishes of the tournament.The victory gave the Renegades their first win of the WBBL season 12, while the Hurricanes remained without a win after three matches and at the bottom of the standings.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
